title: Azmeri Spirit Stacking
intro: A high-investment Atlas farming strategy that snowballs Azmeri Spirits to extreme counts, then dumps the swarm into Rogue Exiles, Summoning Circles, Essences and premium Strongboxes for big Item Rarity payouts (Mageblood, Headhunter, Hinekora's Lock, Mirrors). Spirits possess nearby monsters and become Empowered 50%–300% by the influence of the monster they ride; they only move while tethered close to you and dissipate if left too far behind. The whole loop multiplies spirits across four tiers — getting the Atlas tree, Hilda notables and tablets right is what makes it work. ⚠️ This is a min-max endgame strategy, not a beginner sheet: expect ~200 Divine of build investment and ~7 Divine per map of tablets. Verify exact node wording and numbers in-game before committing.

sections.heading: The Spirits (Azmerian Wisps)
sections.blurb: Azmerian wisps flee from you and possess nearby monsters. A possessed normal becomes "Wisp-Touched"; a fully-possessed rare/unique is "Haunted by the Wisp" and drops a Talisman. Wisps get Empowered (50%–300%) by the monster they ride and pass their absorbed value along the kill chain. There are four varieties — Wild, Vivid, Primal, Sacred — and for this strategy you push Vivid spawn chance hardest while hunting the two Sacred sub-types, which are the real multipliers.

rows: The bread-and-butter loot multiplier for this strategy: +100% crit chance and +100% evasion, faster move/skill speed when fully possessed. Push its spawn chance hard (Unseen Rivers, see Atlas tree).
Wisp-Touched gain stun buildup, toughness and armour; ~200% increased Rarity of items dropped. Good for targeted Strength-based drop pools.
~80% increased Damage plus cold / poison / freeze mechanics; superior for sustained-damage, Intelligence-based conversions. Examples: Owl, Serpent, Primate.
The high-value tier: highest Rarity increases and Rare → Unique boss transformations. Comes as two sub-types, Fox and Rabbit (see below) — find them early.

cards.title: Fox tactics
cards.body: Feed spirits in small pairs to convert several Rares into Uniques, OR ignore the Fox entirely and recover its spirit later by killing the possessed mob. Either way it ends up as a Rarity bomb.

cards.title: Rabbit tactics
cards.body: Feed 4–5 spirits into the same mob. If a revive procs, the multiplication goes nuclear. NEVER clear Strongboxes while a Rabbit is alive — funnel spirits through it instead.

sections.heading: Atlas Passive Tree — Mandatory Nodes
sections.blurb: These are the load-bearing nodes. Spec spirit spawn chance and the Powerful-Boss "Overlord" nodes first, then Rarity.

rows: 100% increased chance of Azmeri Spirits — the core node.
Monsters possessed by Sacred Spirits also possess another random Spirit.
Areas with Powerful Map Bosses contain an additional Azmeri Spirit.
Areas with Powerful Map Bosses contain an additional Rogue Exile.
25% chance to duplicate Corrupted Essence monsters when released.
Ezomyte Cities count as Grass Areas.
Vaal Cities count as Forest Areas.
15% increased Rare Monsters in Forest Areas.
5% chance to upgrade Greater Currencies to Perfect in Grass Areas.
25% chance Shrine Buffs apply to the Boss for additional reward.

cards.title: Spirits do not dissipate
cards.body: Slower runs, but spirits never decay if left behind — guaranteed stacking. The safe default.

cards.title: Spirits have 50% increased Movement Speed
cards.body: Faster but riskier — spirits can outrun you and scatter. Pick this OR the no-dissipate node, by playstyle.

cards.title: Call of the Spirit
cards.body: 10% chance Forest Areas become Rogue Exile Hunting Grounds — more Exiles to dump spirits into.

cards.title: Moths to the Flame
cards.body: Summoning Circles have 20% chance to summon an Azmeri Spirit.

cards.title: Curious Spirits
cards.body: Shrines have 10% chance to release an Azmeri Spirit.

cards.title: Exile pairing & traps
cards.body: Uncommon Alliances (10% Exiles in pairs), Famous Locals (15% City Exiles in pairs), Man Trap (10% Essence monsters become Rogue Exiles) — all add more dump targets.

sections.heading: Hilda Atlas Master Notables
sections.blurb: Hilda is the master that gates the spirit-release mechanics. The first two are mandatory; the rest are a payoff-vs-risk choice.

cards.title: Call of the Spirits
cards.body: Possessed Unique monsters guarantee a spirit release on death — keeps the chain alive.

cards.title: Claimed Territories
cards.body: Overlord nodes have a 45% chance to double their effects (more spirits/exiles on Powerful-Boss maps).

cards.title: Soul Eaters + Lethal Adaptation
cards.body: Maximum rewards, but extremely rippy bosses. For confident, tanky builds.

cards.title: Breeding Season + Ancient Inscriptions
cards.body: Balanced profit boost — a safe middle option.

cards.title: Will of the Draíocht
cards.body: Simplified, brain-dead runs — but spirits cannot possess Rares (lower ceiling).

cards.title: Patient Battue
cards.body: Spawns the maximum number of Uniques.

sections.heading: Tablet Setup
sections.blurb: Recommended loadout: 1 Irradiated + 1 Abyss + 2 Overseers. ~7 Divine per map (1 Irradiated, ~2 each Overseer, ~2 Abyss). Mod priority is top-to-bottom.

rows: +1 additional Rogue Exile (mandatory) → Azmeri % chance → 1–2 random mods → Item Rarity % → Summoning Circle % / Essence %
+2 additional Azmeri Spirits (mandatory) → Azmeri % / Exile % → Item Rarity % → Summoning Circle % / Essence %
+1 additional Azmeri Spirit → Abyss mods (e.g. chance for additional Abysses) → Exile % / Summoning Circle % → Item Rarity %

sections.note: Abysses inherit the absorbed-spirit properties of the monsters that spawn from them — feeding spirits in before an Abyss wave triggers more multiplication.

rows: Ezomyte City (Grass), Vaal City (Forest — avoid Temple of the Sun), Faridun

sections.heading: How Multiplication Snowballs
sections.blurb: Four tiers of synergy stacking on top of each other — each tier feeds the next.

rows: Corrupted Lattices (25% Essence-monster duplication) + spirit release on death.
Rogue Exiles absorb and transfer spirits when they kill possessed Rares.
Sacred Sap — Sacred-Spirit mobs possess an additional random spirit.
Rabbit revives loop the previous three tiers, 0–8× per mob.

sections.heading: Strongbox Handling
sections.blurb: Key rule: Strongboxes don't release absorbed spirits — they only "liberate" one native spirit. But the Ambush waves they spawn inherit absorbed-spirit mods, which triggers multiplication. So save the premium boxes for the finale.

cards.title: Clear immediately
cards.body: Large (quantity only), Blacksmith's, Arcane and Armourer's boxes — pop them early so they don't accidentally eat spirits.

cards.title: Researcher's — save
cards.body: Targets Hinekora's Locks and Mirrors. Feed the swarm in as a finale.

cards.title: Jeweller's — save
cards.body: Targets Mageblood and Headhunter.

cards.title: Ornate — save
cards.body: Massive Item Rarity multiplier — boosts all premium drops.

cards.title: Cryptic Key
cards.body: Use it to open a premium box twice when heavily spirit-stacked.

sections.note: ⚠️ Never clear Strongboxes while a Rabbit spirit is alive — funnel spirits through them instead.

sections.heading: In-Map Execution Order
sections.blurb: Streamlined loop. The priority kill order when spirits scatter: locate Azmeri → kill Exiles → kill Summoning Circles → kill Essences → pop premium Strongboxes.

rows: Kill all monsters except Uniques, Essences and premium Strongboxes. Feed nearby Azmeri into Abyss Rares, then kill them.
Find the Rogue Exile carrying the most spirits and kill it.
If 3–4 spirits wander into the boss room, kill the Map Boss to recover them.
Feed the accumulated swarm into Summoning Circle bosses and execute them.
Feed the swarm into Essences first, then funnel the resulting cluster into Researcher's / Ornate / Jeweller's boxes and open them.

sections.note: Boss-kill timing is flexible, but a premature death halts multiplication — keep yourself alive above all.

sections.heading: Build Requirements
sections.blurb: You need an active-control, high-mobility build that can pace itself to preserve Exiles and not accidentally vacuum spirits.

cards.title: Want
cards.body: Active skill control, high mobility, strong single-target and clear, and solid survivability. The author runs a Sweep Martialist with ~200 Divine invested.

cards.title: Avoid
cards.body: Minions, totems, traps, Twister, automatic Mirage Archer and other passive deployables — they kill on their own and break your pacing/spirit control.
